title: Custom Mailer Boxes for Ecommerce: Sizes, Board, Print and Cost
seoTitle: Custom Mailer Boxes for Ecommerce: Size, Board & Cost Guide
metaDescription: How to choose custom mailer boxes for an online store: flute, sizes, inside printing, shipping weight and what really changes the price per box.
excerpt: A mailer box is the first thing your customer touches. Here is how to pick the right board, size and print so it survives the courier, looks good on camera and does not eat your margin.
coverAlt: Open kraft mailer box with a folded garment and paper bag for ecommerce orders
keyTakeaways: E-flute corrugated suits most products under 3 kg; use B-flute or double wall for heavy or fragile items.
Size the box to the product plus 5-10 mm per side to cut board, void fill and dimensional-weight shipping costs.
Inside printing is what customers film; one or two colours inside is a low-cost way to stand out.
Custom mailer boxes start from 100 pieces at Printy Packaging.

sections.heading: Why online brands switch to mailer boxes
sections.body:
When you sell online, the box is your shop window, your shelf and your delivery driver all at once. A plain brown shipper does the job, but it tells the customer nothing about you.

A mailer box is a one-piece corrugated box with a hinged lid that tucks in at the front. No tape is needed to close it, it opens like a gift, and the lid gives you a whole printed panel inside. That combination of strength and presentation is why clothing, skincare, candle and subscription brands use them so much.

They also ship flat. You store a pallet of folded mailers in a corner and fold each one in a few seconds when an order comes in.

sections.heading: Pick the right board first
sections.body: Everything else depends on the board. Mailer boxes are made from corrugated card, and the thickness of the wavy middle layer (the flute) decides how much weight and rough handling the box can take.
sections.tableCaption: Corrugated board options for mailer boxes
sections.table:
Board | Thickness | Best for
E-flute | about 1.5 mm | Clothing, cosmetics, candles, most products under 3 kg
B-flute | about 3 mm | Heavier items, glass jars, bottles, multiple products
E/B double wall | about 4.5 mm | Fragile or heavy orders shipped long distance
Kraft outer | same flutes | Natural brown look, lower print cost, eco message
White outer | same flutes | Bright full-colour printing, premium look

sections.heading: Sizes that work for most stores
sections.body:
The most common money leak is a box that is too big. You pay for board you do not need, you pay for void fill, and carriers charge for the space. Measure your product with its tissue or insert, then add 5 to 10 mm on each side so it slides in without rattling.

Most couriers, including UPS and FedEx, price parcels by dimensional weight: length x width x height divided by a set number. Cutting a centimetre or two from a box can move an order into a cheaper price band, and that saving repeats on every single shipment.

Inside size (inches) | Inside size (cm) | Good for
6 x 4 x 2 | 15 x 10 x 5 | Jewellery, skincare minis, accessories
8 x 6 x 3 | 20 x 15 x 7.5 | Candles, single cosmetics, small gifts

12 x 9 x 4 | 30 x 23 x 10 | Hoodies, folded clothing, kits
14 x 10 x 4 | 35 x 25 x 10 | Larger apparel, multi-item orders

sections.heading: Inside printing: the part people film
sections.body:
Customers open the lid on camera far more than they photograph the outside. That inside panel is the cheapest place to make a strong impression.

Ideas that work well: a thank-you line, your social handle, a pattern in your brand colour, or care instructions for the product. Keep it simple. One or two colours inside usually looks more deliberate than a busy full-colour print, and it costs less.

If the budget is tight, print inside only and keep the outside plain kraft. It ships anonymously, which some customers prefer, and the reveal still feels special.

sections.heading: What changes the price per box
sections.body:
Mailer pricing is not a mystery once you know the levers. In order of impact:

Quantity. Setup costs (printing plates, cutting die) are spread over the order, so 1,000 boxes cost much less per box than 100. Ask for prices at two or three quantities before you decide.

Size and board. Bigger boxes and double-wall board use more material.

Print coverage and sides. Full-colour on both sides costs more than one colour on the outside.

Finishing. Matte or gloss lamination, spot UV and foil add a step each. They look great on retail boxes, but on a shipper that gets handled by couriers, a simple matte finish is usually enough.

Inserts. A custom cardboard insert holds products in place and replaces loose fill. It adds a little cost but often saves on breakages and returns.

sections.heading: Common mistakes to avoid
sections.body:
Choosing the thickest board to feel premium. Thick board makes the box heavier and more expensive to ship, and customers rarely notice the difference.

Designing before you have a dieline. Ask for the dieline (the flat template) first, then place your artwork on it so logos do not land on a fold.

Forgetting the seal. Mailers close without tape, but for shipping you may still want a branded sticker or tear strip so customers can tell the box was not opened.

Ordering one size for everything. Two or three sizes usually cover a whole catalogue and cut shipping costs across the board.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a mailer box and a shipping box?
faqs.answer: A shipping box (regular slotted carton) is taped shut and is built only for transport. A mailer box has a hinged lid with front tuck flaps, closes without tape and is designed to be opened by the customer as part of the brand experience.

faqs.question: Which flute is best for ecommerce mailer boxes?
faqs.answer: E-flute (about 1.5 mm) is the most common choice because it is light, prints well and protects most products under 3 kg. Use B-flute or double wall for heavier or fragile items.

faqs.question: Can I print inside a mailer box?
faqs.answer: Yes. Inside printing is one of the most popular options because it is what customers see and film when they open the lid. One or two colours inside is a cost-effective way to stand out.
